title: Nonunique nearest stable complex quadratics
description:
For every fixed positive-definite real coefficient inner product, unstable complex quadratics with at least two distinct attained global nearest closed-left-half-plane stable quadratics occur arbitrarily close to z^2, both in monic coefficient space and in the full exact-degree coefficient space. A limiting normal has cubic support against a quartic squared displacement, disproving stable-set prox-regularity; compact localization ensures full-degree global attainment. The same obstruction disproves set prox-regularity of the whole abscissa epigraph. The monic quadratic abscissa nevertheless is function prox-regular at the origin relative to each finite limiting subgradient, with constants depending on that subgradient in the real Euclidean coefficient metric.

This gives a negative answer in degree two to Lewis's historical question about the stable complex monic set. The later Oberwolfach Question1 omits the coefficient field, normalization and metric; its complex convention is explicitly qualified. The note credits Bottema and Kirillov-Overton classical stability-boundary geometry, Burke-Overton/Lewis first-order root analysis, the Poliquin-Rockafellar-Thibault projection characterization, and earlier nearest-polynomial approximation work of Moses-Liu and Orban de Xivry. No real-only or all-degree classification, explicit unstable input and minimizing pair, general nonlinear parameter-metric transfer, firstness or present-day openness guarantee is claimed. The limiting support covector is horizontal; the representing normal vector need not be horizontal in mixed coefficient-height metrics.

The verification archive supplies the complete standalone LaTeX source, a Python-standard-library verifier with 2,005 exact rational assertions and complete expected output, deterministic high-precision function-boundary controls, authored source and bounded-priority notes, publication metadata, license and file hashes.
